Peak plasma con- centrations are reached about 2 hours after oral doses; methyl- phenidate undergoes extensive first-pass metabolism. Protein binding is low. It is excreted as metabolites mainly in the urine with small amounts appearing in the faeces; less than 1% appears in the urine as unchanged methylphenidate. The major metabo- lite is ritalinic acid (2-phenyl-2-piperidyl acetic acid). The plas- ma elimination half-life is about 2 hours. Methylphenidate is dis- tributed into breast milk. ◊ References. 1. Uses and Administration Methylphenidate hydrochloride is a central stimulant and indi- rect-acting sympathomimetic with actions and uses similar to those of dexamfetamine (p.2154). It is used in the treatment of narcolepsy (p.2148) and as an adjunct to psychological, educa- tional, and social measures in the treatment of hyperactivity dis- orders in children.
